questions.q: What makes a Payables invoice distribution eligible to become a mass addition candidate?
options: It is coded to an asset clearing account and has been validated and accounted
It is coded to a normal expense account
It is paid in cash rather than by check
It is entered by an Asset Accounting Manager specifically
questions.explain: Only validated, accounted invoice distributions coded to a GL account flagged as an asset clearing account are eligible for Create Mass Additions.

questions.q: What does the Create Mass Additions process do?
options: It immediately creates a fully depreciating asset
It scans for eligible invoice distributions and sends them to the Fixed Assets interface table
It closes the current depreciation period
It deletes invoice distributions from Payables
questions.explain: Create Mass Additions, run from Payables, sends eligible distributions into a separate Fixed Assets interface table as mass addition candidates.

questions.q: Does a mass addition line sitting in the interface table mean an asset already exists?
options: Yes, it immediately becomes a depreciating asset
Yes, but only in tax books
No, the line is discarded automatically
No, it is only a candidate awaiting review before it can become an asset
questions.explain: A mass addition in the interface table is only a candidate; it still needs to be reviewed and posted before it becomes an actual depreciating asset.

questions.q: What information does a mass addition line typically carry over from Payables?
options: Only the GL date
The employee assigned to the asset
The vendor, invoice number, description, amount, and GL date
The asset's physical location
questions.explain: A mass addition carries useful context from the originating invoice, including vendor, invoice number, description, amount, and GL date.

questions.q: Why do mature implementations rely on mass additions for most new assets rather than manual entry?
options: Because manual entry is disabled once mass additions are configured
Because mass additions do not require an invoice at all
Because it avoids retyping financial data Payables already captured correctly
Because tax books cannot accept manually added assets
questions.explain: Mass additions let financial data be captured once in Payables and flow into Assets automatically, avoiding duplicate manual entry.
